references.text: Moses stretches out his staff as an instrument of God's power, just as he did with other plagues in Egypt.
Moses stretches out his staff over Egypt to bring another plague: locusts.
Moses stretches out his hand over the sea, and the Lord uses natural forces to carry out His will.
The Lord sends hail from heaven as a means of judgment, just as He did in Egypt.
The Lord thunders from heaven and sends hail and flames of fire as signs of His power and judgment.
The psalmist recalls the plague of hail in Egypt where the Lord destroyed the vines and sycamore trees with hail.
The psalm describes how the Lord gave them hail instead of rain and flaming fire in their land.
Isaiah prophesies about the Lord's judgment with thunder, hail, and consuming fire.
Ezekiel prophesies about God's judgment with hail and fire, similar to the elements in the plague of hail.
Revelation describes hail and fire mixed with blood being thrown on the earth, an eschatological echo of Egypt's plagues.
Great hail from heaven falls upon people as part of God's final judgment.
The same gesture ('stretching out toward heaven') is used to initiate opposite phenomena (hail/fire versus darkness) as part of the plagues.
Both show Moses' hand gesture over a natural phenomenon that triggers God's judgment on the Egyptians.
A parallel in the use of the staff to transform elements of the earth into a plague.
Highlights the recurring pattern where God's command to use the staff leads to plagues.
Parallel in how the raising of the staff initiates various types of judgments over Egypt's nature.
